headline: DLSS Rendering, Rebuilt in Vulkan
lede: OpenDLSS-NR recreates Nvidia’s neural rendering network in portable Vulkan code, claiming byte-for-byte agreement across its 71-block FP8 model. The implementation opens the execution path to inspection while leaving model weights, licensing, and demanding hardware outside the box.

headline: Google Tests Argon Behind Closed Doors
lede: Gemini 4 Argon is aimed at long-horizon coding, research, and cyber defense, with a million-token output limit and ambitions for difficult technical work. Google is holding back broad access while it wrestles with prompt injection, agent security, and the consequences of a model built to find vulnerabilities.

headline: OpenAI Takes Aim at Chip Design
lede: OpenAI and Synopsys are joining forces on an agent that can operate electronic-design tools, iterate through constraints, and optimize semiconductor layouts. The promise is accelerated engineering; the immediate question is whether chipmakers will trust a hosted system with their most sensitive designs.
pullquote: The harder the chip problem becomes, the more consequential the question of who gets to operate the tools.

headline: A Book of Shapes for the Browser
lede: Book of Shapes turns simple generative rules into a library of editable SVG patterns. Tweak the geometry, borrow a motif, or drop a lightweight piece of procedural texture into the next page or presentation.

headline: The Secret Satellites That Listened Below
lede: Newly declassified records trace URSALA, RAQUEL, and FARRAH from improvised hitchhiker payloads into long-lived systems for locating radar and electronic emissions. Their story follows Cold War signals intelligence from distant national agencies to operators in the field, carried through low Earth orbit.

headline: How Iron Unmade the Bronze Age Order
lede: The collapse of the Bronze Age was not one catastrophe but a change in the economics of power. As iron drew weapons and tools away from scarce, tightly controlled tin routes, the material basis of empire began to fragment.

headline: The Brain Computes in Traveling Waves
lede: Intracranial recordings reveal planar, source, sink, and spiral waves moving through the brain during memory tasks. Rotating patterns appeared especially often during navigation and recall, suggesting a dynamic coordination system whose computational role remains to be established.

headline: Before Pixels, Operators Read the Wall
lede: Industrial dashboards once made complex systems legible through lamps, counters, switches, labels, and touchable modules. In museums across Germany and Poland, these panels preserve a quieter lesson in interface design: status must be visible, and control must make sense under pressure.

headline: Why Decimal Addition Draws Checkerboards
lede: Adding values that look like cents exposes the hidden choreography of binary rounding, ulps, significand parity, and decimal printing. This deep dive maps the resulting patterns and shows how tools such as 2Sum can recover the errors floating point normally conceals.

headline: Magnitude Tunes Local Agents to Their Hardware
lede: Magnitude is a Rust inference engine for concurrent, long-running local agents, compiling and autotuning GPU kernels for each device. Its early benchmarks point to faster decoding and lower memory use in selected configurations, while broader hardware coverage and real-session comparisons remain unfinished specifications.
